scenario: Gas detector in process area reads 12% LEL. Workers are still operating nearby equipment.
expected_decision: STOP WORK AUTHORITY — Lower Explosive Limit Threshold Exceeded

scenario: A worker asks if it is safe to mix two unlabelled chemical drums found in the storage area. No SDS or chemical identity is available.
expected_decision: INSUFFICIENT INFORMATION — Cannot determine safe decision without verified evidence
evidence_sources: Chemical identity must be confirmed before any compatibility assessment

scenario: An industrial hygienist measures a worker noise dose of 110% PEL after 6 hours in a fabrication workshop.
expected_decision: CORRECTIVE ACTION REQUIRED — Noise Dose Exceeds Permissible Exposure Limit

scenario: An electrician is working on a 415V panel without performing lockout/tagout. The panel remains energized.
expected_decision: LOTO REQUIRED — Stop Work on Energized Equipment
evidence_sources: NFPA 70E — Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace

scenario: Atmospheric test in a storage tank shows 16% oxygen before confined space entry.
expected_decision: ENTRY DENIED — Unsafe Atmospheric Condition

scenario: A worker is observed performing roof repairs at 5 metres height without a harness or fall arrest system in place.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Fall Protection Required: No person shall work at height without 100% tied-off fall arrest system

scenario: Computed safety factor for a crane lift is 3.2. The operation is classified as a critical lift requiring a minimum safety factor of 5.0.
expected_decision: STOP WORK AUTHORITY — Insufficient Safety Factor

scenario: An excavation 2.8 metres deep has been dug in Type C soil with vertical walls and no shoring or sloping applied.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Excavation protection required: shoring, sloping, or shielding must be installed before any personnel enter

scenario: A pressure vessel is operating without a pressure relief valve. Operating pressure is 12 bar and design pressure is 10 bar.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Pressure exceeds design limit and no relief device is installed; immediate shutdown and inspection required
evidence_sources: ASME BPVC Section VIII — Pressure Vessels

scenario: Atmospheric monitoring in a confined space shows 22.8% oxygen. Workers ask if entry is safe.
expected_decision: ENTRY DENIED — Oxygen enriched atmosphere (>23.5%) creates elevated fire and explosion risk. Ventilate and retest before entry.
evidence_sources: NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards

scenario: A production operator removed a machine guard to clear a jam and is continuing to operate the press without replacing the guard.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Machine must not operate without guards; replace guarding before restarting production

scenario: A radiation worker's dosimeter reads 18 mSv for the month. Monthly limit is 20 mSv. Supervisor asks if work can continue.
expected_decision: Apply ALARP review: remaining dose budget is 2 mSv; restrict high-exposure tasks and apply additional shielding before continuing work
evidence_sources: IAEA Safety Standards — Occupational Radiation Protection
NRC 10 CFR 20 — Standards for Protection Against Radiation

scenario: Workers cleaning a bird roosting area on an industrial roof without respiratory protection or infection controls.
expected_decision: Apply biological hazard controls: N95 or P100 respirator, disposable coveralls, gloves, and wetting agent before work; respiratory protection is mandatory

scenario: Outdoor workers in a desert location are working during peak afternoon heat with WBGT of 32°C. No rest breaks or hydration schedule in place.
expected_decision: Implement heat stress controls: mandatory rest/work schedule (45 min work, 15 min shade), hydration at 250 mL per 15 minutes, acclimatization programme for new workers
evidence_sources: NIOSH Criteria for a Recommended Standard — Occupational Exposure to Heat and Hot Environments
ISO 7933 — Ergonomics of the Thermal Environment

scenario: Fine-Kinney risk assessment for a maintenance task yields a risk score of 500. Work is about to commence.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Extreme Risk Level Detected
evidence_sources: Risk score >= 400 = Extreme: Stop Work required

scenario: Industrial hygiene monitoring shows a worker has a silica TWA of 0.08 mg/m³ against an OEL of 0.05 mg/m³.
expected_decision: CORRECTIVE ACTION REQUIRED — TWA Exceeds Occupational Exposure Limit

scenario: Combined confined space entry and welding task in an area where gas monitoring shows 7% LEL.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Hot work is prohibited below 10% LEL threshold but gas presence requires immediate investigation. Ventilate until LEL reads zero before any hot work permit is issued.

scenario: An electrician is working on a 33kV switchgear without appropriate arc flash PPE. The switchgear has not been isolated.
expected_decision: LOTO REQUIRED — Stop Work on Energized Equipment

scenario: During excavation, a worker strikes an unmarked underground cable. The cable type and voltage are unknown.
expected_decision: INSUFFICIENT INFORMATION — Cannot determine safe decision without verified evidence
evidence_sources: Excavation must stop until cable is identified and declared safe by qualified authority

scenario: Crane lift scheduled outdoors with ambient temperature 44°C, workers required to lift heavy rigging in full PPE without cooling breaks.
expected_decision: Proceed with lift only with modified heat stress controls: mandatory cooling breaks every 20 minutes, designated shaded rest area, buddy system monitoring, and pre-lift hydration check

scenario: A near miss involving a dropped tool from height was observed but the supervisor chose not to report it because no one was injured.
expected_decision: Near miss must be reported: all near misses have reporting obligations and are key leading safety indicators. Failure to report constitutes a compliance violation.

scenario: A worker suffered a fractured finger when it was caught in a conveyor belt. Apply root cause analysis to determine causal factors.
expected_decision: Initiate RCA using 5-Why method: investigate machine guarding adequacy, LOTO compliance, JSA currency, worker training records, and supervisory oversight

scenario: An audit finding from 6 months ago was closed as 'corrective action completed' but the same hazard condition has been found again during a follow-up inspection.
expected_decision: Reopen CAPA: verify that root cause was correctly identified; implement effectiveness review process; escalate repeated findings to management for systemic review
evidence_sources: ISO 9001:2015 Clause 10.2 — Nonconformity and Corrective Action

scenario: A serious electrical incident occurred at Site A, but management has not shared the lessons learned with other sites in the same company.
expected_decision: Issue lessons learned bulletin across all sites immediately; present at next HSSE meeting; verify similar hazards are controlled at each site
evidence_sources: IOGP Process Safety — Incident Sharing Guidelines

scenario: Site emergency evacuation drill has not been conducted in 14 months. A new emergency response plan has been written but not tested.
expected_decision: Schedule and conduct full emergency evacuation drill within 30 days; debrief all personnel; verify emergency response plan is current and roles are understood

scenario: First aid kit inspection reveals 40% of items are expired or missing. The site has 35 workers. No registered first aider is on duty this shift.
expected_decision: Immediately restock first aid kit to full compliance; ensure qualified first aider is present on every shift; review first aid needs assessment for site population
evidence_sources: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151 — Medical Services and First Aid
HSE First Aid at Work Regulations

scenario: Large-scale chlorine gas release from a chemical plant. Multiple workers are reporting eye and respiratory irritation. Muster point is 150 metres from the release.
expected_decision: Activate Incident Command System: declare emergency, evacuate to upwind muster point, alert emergency services, initiate shelter-in-place protocol for nearby community if required

scenario: A worker missed 3 days of work following a back injury from manual handling. How should this be classified?
expected_decision: Classify as Lost Time Injury (LTI): report to regulator per local requirements; enter in TRIR calculation; initiate RCA and CAPA; review manual handling assessment for the task

scenario: A light vehicle reversed into a pedestrian in a laydown yard. No injuries but the vehicle speed exceeded 10 km/h in a 5 km/h zone. Conduct RCA.
expected_decision: RCA required: investigate speed management controls, physical segregation of pedestrians and vehicles, CCTV review, driver training records, and site traffic management plan compliance

scenario: Fire at the diesel fuel storage bund. Fire suppression system has been activated but flame is continuing. Two workers are unaccounted for.
expected_decision: Activate full emergency response: call emergency services immediately; do not re-enter search area until fire brigade declares safe; roll call all personnel at muster; activate incident command
evidence_sources: NFPA 30 — Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code

scenario: A supervisor reports that a worker has displayed signs of severe psychological distress including threats to self-harm. What immediate action is required?
expected_decision: Activate mental health emergency protocol: remove person from hazardous work area immediately; ensure they are not alone; contact occupational health or emergency services; provide peer support resources

scenario: Site HSSE data shows no management leadership HSSE walkarounds have been conducted in 45 days. HSSE incident rate has increased 30% compared to the previous period.
expected_decision: Escalate to senior management: immediately reinstate HSSE leadership walkabouts (minimum weekly); conduct management review meeting; develop HSSE improvement action plan with measurable targets

scenario: Contractor is about to start welding work inside a live process area without a hot work permit.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Hot work permit required before any ignition source is introduced into a process area; isolate ignition sources until valid PTW is issued
evidence_sources: Hot Work Permit to Work Procedure

scenario: Maintenance technician is about to perform servicing on a pump that drives a hazardous chemical line. No LOTO procedure has been applied.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — LOTO must be applied to all energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, chemical) before maintenance begins; verify zero energy state before entry

scenario: A team is about to perform a task that has never been done at this site before. No Job Safety Analysis has been prepared.
expected_decision: Stop work: conduct JSA before starting. Identify all hazards step-by-step, assign controls at each step, obtain supervisor approval before proceeding
evidence_sources: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 8.1 — Operational Planning and Control

scenario: During a BBS observation, a worker is seen lifting a 30 kg object alone using a bent-back posture without mechanical assistance.
expected_decision: Intervene: correct lifting technique immediately; assess if task requires mechanical handling aid; update JSA and manual handling risk assessment; provide refresher training

scenario: Workers in a grinding area are relying entirely on earplugs as the noise control measure. Noise levels are 98 dBA. Engineering controls have not been assessed.
expected_decision: Review hierarchy of controls: engineering controls (noise enclosure, damping, isolation) must be assessed before relying solely on PPE. PPE is last resort, not primary control.

scenario: Workers performing concrete cutting need respiratory protection against silica dust. What respiratory protection should be selected?
expected_decision: Select minimum N95 respirator (half-face APF 10) for incidental silica exposure; P100 half-face (APF 10) or powered air-purifying respirator for heavy cutting; fit test required for all tight-fitting respirators

scenario: A subcontractor worker arrived on site and went directly to work without completing mandatory HSSE induction training.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — No person may enter a controlled work site without completing mandatory HSSE induction. Remove worker from site immediately and reschedule induction.

scenario: A work crew is using a confined space entry procedure that was last revised 5 years ago. Site conditions have changed significantly since that revision.
expected_decision: Stop work pending document review: outdated procedure must be revised to reflect current site conditions; work shall not proceed using superseded documents

scenario: Confined space entry task requires a dedicated attendant at the entry point. The only available person for the task is also assigned as the entrant.
expected_decision: Stop work: confined space entry requires a separate, dedicated attendant who does not enter the space. Obtain additional resource before work commences.

scenario: Fine-Kinney risk assessment gives a score of 450 for a maintenance task on an energized high-voltage switchboard.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Extreme Risk Level Detected
evidence_sources: Risk score ≥ 400 = Extreme risk: work cessation mandatory

scenario: A new chemical solvent is being introduced to the painting process. No hazard identification has been performed for this new substance.
expected_decision: Stop use: obtain SDS, conduct HAZID for new chemical, update chemical register and risk assessment, train workers on hazards before chemical is introduced to workplace

scenario: Engineering team has modified a feed pipe diameter in a chemical process without raising a Management of Change request.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Process modification without MOC approval is prohibited. Raise MOC immediately, conduct HAZOP review of change, update P&IDs and operating procedures before restart

scenario: A new contractor is mobilising to site. Their HSSE prequalification has not been reviewed or approved.
expected_decision: STOP mobilisation: contractor must complete HSSE prequalification assessment and receive approval before any personnel are allowed on site

scenario: An operator is observed using a mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) without the required MEWP operator certification.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Operator must hold valid certification for MEWP operation. Remove from task immediately and arrange certified replacement operator

scenario: Night shift started work on a plant turnaround without receiving a formal handover briefing from the outgoing day shift. Critical isolation status was not communicated.
expected_decision: Stop all non-emergency work: conduct immediate handover briefing to confirm isolation status and ongoing work conditions before night shift activities resume
